item.title: NEW: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Services After Supply Chain Attack on M365
item.description:
Headline: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Services After Supply Chain Attack on M365

Summary:
ConnectWise has suspended its Cloud Backup services following a sophisticated supply chain attack. Threat actors compromised an application credential, gaining unauthorized access to the Microsoft 365 tenants of numerous Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and their customers. The attack, which bypasses user-level MFA, allowed for broad data access and privilege escalation. ConnectWise has disabled the affected application identities and is investigating the incident, which Microsoft has classified as an active supply chain attack.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Supply Chain Attack, Cloud Security, Cyberattack

Meta Description: ConnectWise has suspended its cloud backup services due to a supply chain attack where a compromised application credential was used to breach Microsoft 365 tenants.

item.description:
Headline: OpenCode Breach Exposes OpenAI, Anthropic API Keys, Leads to Fraud

Summary:
The open-source AI coding agent OpenCode has disclosed a security breach that exposed user API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. The incident, which affected 1.4% of its Console users, resulted from unauthorized access to a legacy system. Attackers used the stolen keys in a 'distillation attack,' running up significant fraudulent charges on user accounts to likely train their own AI models. OpenCode has notified affected users and advised them to revoke and replace the compromised keys.

Severity: High

Categories: Data Breach, Cloud Security, Other

Meta Description: A security breach at OpenCode, an open-source AI agent, has exposed user API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, leading to fraudulent charges for users.

item.description:
Headline: CISA Warns of Actively Exploited BeyondTrust Flaw Used by Chinese APT

Summary:
CISA has added a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The flaw, which allows for arbitrary file operations, has been actively exploited as a zero-day since August 2026 by a suspected China-linked espionage group, ARMORY CASTLE. The attackers use the flaw to gain initial access, escalate privileges, and deploy custom malware. BeyondTrust has released patches, and CISA urges all organizations to update immediately.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Threat Actor, Patch Management

Meta Description: CISA warns that a critical vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764) is being actively exploited by a China-linked APT group. Patching is urgent.

item.title: UPDATE: China-Linked Group Exploits BeyondTrust Zero-Day in Espionage Attacks
item.description:
Headline: China-Linked Group Exploits BeyondTrust Zero-Day in Espionage Attacks

Summary:
A China-linked cyber espionage group known as Armory Castle (UNC5221) has been exploiting a critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-102764, in BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances. The flaw, with a CVSS score of 9.3, allows unauthenticated attackers to gain root-level control. The campaign, which began in late August 2026, involved deploying custom malware like the SAWFLY web shell and BARECLAW tunneler to achieve persistence, escalate privileges, and exfiltrate credentials from the device's secrets database. The attackers also wiped logs to cover their tracks. BeyondTrust has released patches and urges self-hosted customers to update immediately, rebuild compromised appliances from clean images, and rotate all associated credentials. The campaign targeted legal, technology, and government sectors, consistent with intelligence collection motives.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Threat Actor, Cyberattack

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: A China-linked cyber espionage group is exploiting a critical zero-day (CVE-2026-102764) in BeyondTrust Remote Support to gain root control and steal data.

item.title: UPDATE: Cyber-Physical Attack Hits 700 French Supermarkets via Refrigerators
item.description:
Headline: Cyber-Physical Attack Hits 700 French Supermarkets via Refrigerators

Summary:
A large-scale cyber-physical attack has crippled over 700 supermarkets across France, including major chains like Coopérative U and Carrefour Market. Attackers remotely manipulated Danfoss refrigeration controllers, causing them to overheat to temperatures as high as 50°C (122°F). This act of sabotage resulted in massive spoilage of fresh and frozen food, operational shutdowns, and even small fires. The attack exploited vulnerabilities in obsolete equipment that was no longer receiving security updates. The incident, which has also affected supply chains in several other European countries and the US, highlights the severe real-world consequences of unsecured Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and IoT devices in critical infrastructure.

Severity: High

Categories: Cyberattack, Industrial Control Systems, Supply Chain Attack

Article Type: NewsArticle

Meta Description: A cyberattack on Danfoss refrigeration controllers at 700 French supermarkets caused massive food spoilage and fires, highlighting risks in unsecured OT systems.
